chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Musa ibn Imran, when he prayed, would not turn away (from prayer) until he pressed his right cheek to the ground and his left cheek to the ground.' Ishaq said: 'And I saw among my forefathers one who did that.' Muhammad ibn Sinan said: 'He means Musa, in the forecourt (of the mosque), in the middle of the night.'

key_terms.الْحِجْرُ: The forecourt or enclosed area of a mosque
key_terms.يَنْفَتِلْ: To turn away or conclude (from prayer)

ai.seo_question: What was the specific manner of prostration described for Musa ibn Imran during his prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the profound humility (khushu') of Musa ibn Imran, detailing his unique practice of keeping both cheeks pressed to the ground during prostration, a sign of total submission. Muhammad ibn Sinan specifies this occurred during night prayers (Tahajjud) in the forecourt, emphasizing the spiritual intensity of nocturnal worship. This practice is often cited by Shia scholars to illustrate the ideal of complete physical and spiritual devotion in Salah, distinguishing it from mere ritualistic performance.
